State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
M/S Carewell, vs 1. Ajay Saini on 26 November, 2013
STATE
CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, 

 

U.T., CHANDIGARH 

 

 

 
 
 
 

First
 Appeal No. 
 
 
 

: 
 
 
 

444 of 2013 
 
 
 
 
 

Date of Institution 
 
 
 

:

Date of Decision

M/s Carewell, Plot No.
F-359, Industrial Area, Phase 8B, Mohali, through its Manager. 

 

  

 

Appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 

 V e r s u s 

 

  

 

1.
Ajay Saini son of Sh. Dharampal Saini,
Resident of House No.1017-A, Sector 41-B, Chandigarh. 

 

..Respondent No.1/complainant 

 

  

 

2. Jain Electronics, SCO
86, Sector 40-C, Chandigarh. (Service of respondent no.2 dispensed
with, vide order dated 18.11.2013) 

 

..Respondent No.2/Opposite Party No.1 

 

  

 

3.
M/s Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing
Company Limited, Plot No.A-49, Industrial Area, Phase VIII-B, Mohali. 

 

..Respondent
No.3/Opposite Party No.3 

 

  

 

Appeal under
Section 15
of the Consumer
Protection Act, 1986. 

 

  

 

BEFORE: JUSTICE SHAM SUNDER (RETD.), PRESIDENT. 

 

 MR. DEV RAJ, MEMBER.
Argued
by: Sh. Kamal Kant Verma, Advocate for the
appellant.
Sh.
Mohit Malik, Advocate Proxy, for Sh. Ajay Saini, Advocate for respondent no.1.
Sh. Gangadharan P. V. Manager (Legal and Admin.), Authorized Representative for respondent
no.3.
Service
of respondent no.2 dispensed with, vide order dated
18.11.2013.
PER JUSTICE SHAM SUNDER (RETD.), PRESIDENT 

 

 This appeal is directed against
the order dated 11.07.2013, rendered by the District Consumer Disputes
Redressal Forum-I, U.T., Chandigarh (hereinafter to be called as the District
Forum only), vide which, it partly accepted the complaint, filed by the
complainant (now respondent no.1) and directed Opposite Party No.2 (now the
appellant), as under:-
For the reasons
recorded above, we find merit in the complaint and the same is partly
allowed. OP-2 is directed: -
i) To handover
the washing machine to the complainant in proper working orders to his
satisfaction with a fresh warranty of one year.
ii) It is also
directed to make the payment of Rs.10,000/- to the complainant towards
harassment, mental agony on account of deficiency in service.
iii) To pay
Rs.5,000/- towards litigation expenses to the complainant.
This order shall be
complied with by OP-2 within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of
its certified copy, failing which OP-2 shall refund the amount of Rs.18,500/-
alongwith interest @9% p.a. from the date of purchase of the washing machine
till realization, apart from making the payment of compensation and
litigation.
2.     
 The complaint
against Opposite Parties No.1 and 3 (now respondents no.2 and 3), was
dismissed, by the District Forum.
3.     
 The facts, in
brief, are that the complainant purchased a washing machine, make GWF700 FSCPS
7.0KG, from Opposite Party No.1 authorized dealer of Godrej & Boyce
Manufacturing Company Limited/ Opposite Party No.3, for a sum of Rs.18,500/-
(inclusive of VAT), on 21.03.2012, vide bill, photocopy whereof is Annexure
C/1. The said washing machine carried a warranty of 24 months, from the date of
its purchase. At the time of purchase of the said washing machine, Opposite
Party No.1 assured the complainant, that the same was of best quality, and would
function properly. It was also assured by Opposite Party No.1, that, in case of any defect, in the said washing
machine, it could be replaced with a new one, of the same description.
4.     
 After five
months of purchase of the said washing machine, the complainant noticed
inherent defects, in the same. On 19.09.2012, the complainant visited the
premises of Opposite Party No.1, with a complaint with regard to the defects,
in the washing machine. The representative of Opposite Party No.1, asked the
complainant, to visit its authorized Workshop/Service Centre i.e. Opposite
Party No.2, for rectification of defects, in the said machine. The complainant
contacted Opposite Party No.2 on 21.09.2012, which sent its representative,
namely Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, to his residence. The washing machine was checked by
Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, but he was unable to
remove the defects, in the same, being beyond his reach/control, which fact was
acknowledged by him (Sanjeev Kumar), in writing, on the same day (21.09.2012).
5.     
 Thereafter,
on 06.11.2012, after so many complaints, one Sh.Jaswinder Singh, came to the
residence of the complainant, but he also could not find out the defects, in
the washing machine. Thereafter, various complaints were made by the
complainant, as a result whereof, on 08.11.2012, again a representative of
Opposite Party No.2, visited the residence of the complainant, and took the
washing machine with him, for rectification of defects, and a service slip,
Annexure C/2, was issued to him (complainant).
6.     
 It was stated
that the Opposite Parties failed to refund the price of the defective washing
machine. It was further stated that no communication was received from Opposite
Party No.2, regarding the rectification of defects, in the washing machine,
which forced the complainant to buy a new one, on 27.11.2012, vide retail
invoice, copy whereof is Annexure C/3. It was further stated that the Opposite
Parties were many a time, asked to redress the grievance of the complainant,
but to no avail. It was further stated that the aforesaid acts of the Opposite
Parties, amounted to deficiency, in rendering service, as also indulgence into
unfair trade practice. When the grievance of the complainant, was not
redressed, left with no alternative, a complaint under
Section 12
of the Consumer
Protection Act, 1986 (hereinafter to be called as the Act only), was filed,
directing the Opposite Parties, to refund the price of the washing machine,
lying in the workshop of Opposite Party No.2, alongwith interest @9% p.a.; pay compensation,
to the tune of Rs.10,000/-, for mental agony and physical harassment, and cost
of litigation, to the tune of Rs.7,000/-.
7.     
 Opposite
Party No.1, in its written version, admitted that it is the authorized dealer
of Godrej Electronic appliances. It was also admitted that the complainant
purchased the said washing machine, on 21.03.2012, for a sum of Rs.18,500/-. It
was also admitted that the washing machine purchased by the complainant,
carried a warranty for 24 months, from the date of its purchase, for repairs of
the product, free-of-charge. It was also admitted that the complainant
approached Opposite Party No.1, in September, 2012 and his complaint was
forwarded to the Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company Limited/Opposite
Party No.3. It was stated that the complainant was also provided the address of
the authorized Workshop/Service Centre i.e. Opposite Party No.2, for redressal
of his grievance, with regard to the defects, in the washing machine. It was
further stated that the washing machine, was sold to the complainant, in intact
and packed condition. It was further stated that, after sale of the product,
Opposite Party No.1, could not be held liable, for any act and conduct of the
service provider and the manufacturer. It was further stated that neither there
was any deficiency, in rendering service, on the part of Opposite Party No.1,
nor it indulged into unfair trade practice. The remaining averments, were
denied, being wrong.
8.     
 Opposite
Party No.2, in its written version, stated that the complaint with regard to
the washing machine, was received for the first time, on 03.09.2012, regarding
vibrations in the same. It was further stated that leveling was done, in the
washing machine. It was further stated that, for the second time, the shock
absorber of the washing machine was replaced. It was further stated that the
complainant was not satisfied with the work done, on the said washing machine,
and, therefore, Opposite Party No.2, requested Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra,
Technical Department Head of Opposite Party No.3, to diagnose the defect, in
the washing machine. It was further stated that, during the checking of washing
machine by Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra,
it was found that the same was working properly. The complainant was called to
check the washing machine, thoroughly, in the workshop of Opposite Party No.2.
It was further stated that the complainant was not satisfied with the report of
Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra, in respect of the washing machine, in question. It
was further stated that the washing machine was again checked properly, at the
workshop of Opposite party No.2, and the complainant was called for delivery of
the same. Every time, future date was given by the complainant, with different
excuses that he was out of station, busy etc. It was further stated that
finally, notice of this complaint was received by Opposite Party No.2, from the
District Forum. It was further stated that the washing machine had been lying,
in the workshop of Opposite Party No.2, after thorough check up, and was in perfect
working condition, but it was the complainant, who did not turn up, to collect
the same. It was further stated that neither there was any deficiency, in
rendering service, on the part of Opposite Party No.2, nor it indulged into
unfair trade practice. The remaining averments, were denied, being wrong.
9.     
 Opposite Party
No.3, in its written version, reiterated the pleas, taken up by Opposite Party
No.2, in its written version. It was stated that the complainant did not take
the delivery of the washing machine, with an intention to get undue advantage
under the Act. It was further stated that neither there was any deficiency, in
rendering service, on the part of Opposite Party No.3, nor it indulged into
unfair trade practice. The remaining averments, were denied, being wrong.
10.  
 The Parties
led evidence, in support of their case.
11.  
 After hearing
the Counsel for the complainant, Opposite Party No.1, Sh. Raj Kumar, Manager of
Opposite Party No.2, Sh. Gangadharan P.V., Manager (Legal and Admin),
Authorized Representative of Opposite
Party No.3, and, on going through the evidence, and record of the case, the
District Forum, partly accepted the complaint, in the manner, referred to, in
the opening para of the instant order.
12.  
 Feeling
aggrieved, the instant appeal, has been filed by the appellant/Opposite Party
No.2.
13.  
 Service of
respondent no.2/Opposite Party No.1, was dispensed with, by the Commission, on
18.11.2013, as the complaint against it was dismissed by the District Forum.
14.  
 We have heard
the Counsel for the appellant, respondent no.1, Sh. Gangadharan P.V., Manager (Legal
and Admin.), Authorized Representative of respondent no.3, and, have gone
through the evidence, and record of the case, carefully.
15.  
 The Counsel
for the appellant/Opposite Party No.2, submitted that Opposite Party No.2, was
only a Service Provider. He further submitted that the washing machine, in
question, duly repaired, and in perfect working condition, was lying in its
premises, but despite issuance of notice, to the complainant, he was not
picking up the same, with a view to take advantage of the beneficial provisions
of the Act. He further submitted that since Opposite Party No.2, is only a
Service Provider, the direction of the District Forum, to it, for giving a fresh
warranty of one year, was illegal. He further submitted that such a direction,
if any, could only be given to the manufacturer of the said washing machine
i.e. Opposite Party No.3, but the District Forum, did not do so. He further
submitted that there was no deficiency, in rendering service, on the part of
Opposite Party No.2, yet, the District Forum granted compensation, in the sum
of Rs.10,000/-, and litigation expenses, to the tune of Rs.5,000/-. He further
submitted that the District Forum, was also wrong, in coming to the conclusion,
that, in case, the order impugned was not complied with, within 30 days, then
Opposite Party No.2, shall refund the amount of Rs.18,500/-, i.e. the price of
the washing machine, in question, alongwith interest, from the date of purchase
of the same, till realization. He further submitted that the District Forum,
could not grant compensation, twice, once in the sum of Rs.10,000/-, and
secondly by way of refund of amount of the price of washing machine, to the
tune of Rs.18,500/-. He further submitted that the appellant/Opposite Party
No.2, has already complied with the order impugned, within 30 days, from the
date of receipt of a free-of-cost certified copy thereof. He further submitted
that the order of the District Forum, being illegal, is liable to be set aside.
16.  
 On the other
hand, the Counsel for respondent no.1/complainant, submitted that the order impugned
was not complied with, within 30 days, by Opposite Party No.2. He further
submitted that Opposite Party No.2, came to know of the passing of the order
dated 11.07.2013, immediately, after the same was passed, as he was throughout
appearing in the Consumer Complaint, on behalf of Opposite Party No.1, in the
District Forum, against which, the complaint was dismissed. He further
submitted that despite receipt of a free-of-cost certified copy of the order dated 11.07.2013, immediately, after the same
was passed, Opposite Party No.2 did not comply with the same (order), and, on
the other hand, certified copy of the same (order impugned) was again received by it, on 13.09.2013. He further submitted
that the order of the District Forum, being based on correct appreciation of
evidence, and law on the point, does not suffer from any illegality and
perversity, and the same is liable to be upheld.
17.  
 After giving
our thoughtful consideration, to the rival contentions, advanced by the Counsel
for the appellant, respondents no.1 and 3, and the evidence, on record, we are
of the considered opinion, that the appeal is liable to be partly accepted, for
the reasons, to be recorded hereinafter. The factum of purchase of washing
machine, on 21.03.2012, vide retail invoice Annexure C-1, in the sum of
Rs.18,500/-, by the complainant, from Opposite Party No.1 was admitted. It is
also evident, from the evidence, on record,
that the said washing machine carried a warranty of 24 months. However,
it developed defects, in September 2012. One, Mr.Sanjeev Kumar, Mechanic was
deputed by Opposite Party No.2, who visited the residence of the complainant,
for checking the machine, on 21.09.2012. The washing machine was giving noise
while spinning, but Mr. Sanjeev Kumar, Mechanic of Opposite Party No.2, could
not rectify the defect, and communicated with his senior-Mr. Vijay (infact Vinay) Kumar. The affidavits of Sunil Kumar and Vinay Kumar
were not filed by Opposite Party No.2, to belie the assertions made by the
complainant, which were duly supported by him, through his affidavit. There
was, therefore, deficiency, in rendering service, on the part of Opposite Party
No.2, as its mechanics/engineers aforesaid, failed to rectify the defects, in
the said washing machine.
18.  
 Not only
this, when again, a complaint was made by the complainant, with regard to the said
machine, leveling of the same (washing machine) was done, for the first time.
For the second time, the shock absorber of the washing machine was replaced. Mr.
Jaswinder Singh Sanotra, Technical Department Head of M/s Godrej & Boyce
Mfg. Co. Ltd., also checked the machine, and according to him, he found the
same, to be working properly. Neither any document was produced by Opposite
Party No.2 that Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra, Technical Department Head of M/s
Godrej & Boyce Mfg. Co. Ltd., rectified the defects, in the washing
machine, in question, nor his (Mr.
Jaswinder Singh Sanotra) affidavit, that the same (washing machine) was in
proper working condition, was produced, on the record. Under these circumstances, the District Forum
was right, in holding that an adverse inference could be drawn, against
Opposite Party No.2, that had the affidavit of Mr. Jaswinder Singh Sanotra,
aforesaid, been produced, it would not have supported its case. The District
Forum was also right, in holding that there were defects, in the machine, which
were not rectified by the mechanics/engineers of Opposite Party No.2, the
Service Provider, when the complaints were made to it (Opposite Party No.2),
from time to time. The District Forum, was, thus, right in holding that there
was deficiency, in rendering service, on the part of Opposite Party No.2, in
this regard.
19.  
 Coming to the
contention of the Counsel for Opposite Party No.2, that after the defects were
removed, in the washing machine, a notice was sent to the complainant, for
picking up the same, but he did not pick up the same, with a view to take undue
advantage of the beneficial provisions of the Act, it may be stated here, that no
evidence, in respect thereof, was produced by Opposite Party No.2, in the
District Forum. The District Forum, was, thus, right in holding that, in the
absence of any documentary evidence, showing that the notice was issued to the
complainant, for picking up the washing machine, from the premises of Opposite
Party No.2, after the defects therein, had been rectified, its (Opposite Party
No.2) plea could not be said to be correct. The District Forum was, thus, right
in holding that there was a grave deficiency, in rendering service, on the part
of Opposite Party No.2, in this regard also.
20.  
 In our
considered opinion, the District Forum was also right, in coming to the
conclusion, in paragraph number 9 of the impugned order, that the complainant
failed to produce any expert evidence, that there were inherent manufacturing
defects, in the said washing machine. The mere fact that the washing machine, developed
defects, after the same was used by the complainant, for about five months, did
not, in any way, go to prove that the same was suffering from inherent
manufacturing defects. In paragraph number 9, in the impugned order, the
District Forum, was also right, in coming to the conclusion, that since the
complainant failed to prove that there were inherent manufacturing defects, in
the said washing machine, no justifiable ground was made out, to order the refund
of price thereof. The findings of the District Forum, in this regard,
therefore, being correct are affirmed.
21.  
 It may be
stated here, that though the District Forum, came to the conclusion, that the
said washing machine, did not suffer from inherent manufacturing defects, and,
as such, refund of the price thereof, could not be ordered, yet, in its
impugned order, in paragraph number 11, it was directed by it that, in case, the same (order impugned) was not complied
with, by Opposite Party No.2 within a period of 30 days, from the date of
receipt of its certified copy, it shall refund the amount of Rs.18,500/-, being
the price of the same (washing machine) alongwith interest @9% p.a., from the
date of purchase of the same, till realization. This finding of the District Forum, in our considered
opinion, is contrary to the finding, in paragraph number 9 of the impugned
order. This finding of the District Forum, is, thus, set aside.
22.  
 The District
Forum also directed Opposite Party No.2, which is the Service Provider, to give
a fresh warranty to the complainant, in respect of the washing machine, in
question, after handing over the same, to him, in proper working condition, to
his satisfaction. It may be stated here, that Opposite Party No.2, being only the
Service Provider, could not, as per the provisions of law, give fresh warranty.
It is only the manufacturer, which could give fresh warranty. Further, the
District Forum, dismissed the complaint against the manufacturer of the said
machine, i.e. Opposite Party No.3, (now respondent no.3). No appeal was filed
by respondent no.1/complainant, for any direction against Opposite Party No.3, for
issuance of a fresh warranty. The direction/finding of the District Forum, to
this extent, is also set aside.
23.  
 No other
point, was urged, by the Counsel for the appellant, respondent no.1, and Sh.
Gangadharan P.V., Manager (Legal and Admin.), Authorized Representative of
respondent no.3.
24.  
 For the
reasons recorded above, the appeal is partly accepted, with no order as to
costs. The order of the District Forum is modified, in the following manner:
i.   The appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 shall handover the washing machine, in question, to respondent
no.1/complainant, in a proper working condition, after rectifying the defects
therein, within 30 days, from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this
order.
ii.   The appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 shall pay compensation, to the tune of Rs.10,000/-, as awarded by
the District Forum, for deficiency, in rendering service, mental agony and
physical harassment, caused to the complainant.
iii.   The appellant/Opposite
Party No.2 shall pay cost of litigation, to the tune of Rs.5,000/-, as awarded
by the District Forum, to respondent no.1/complainant.
iv.   In case, the amount of
compensation, mentioned in Clause (ii) above, is not paid by the appellant/Opposite
Party No.2, to respondent no.1/complainant, within 30 days, from the date of
receipt of a certified copy of this order, the same shall carry interest @9 P.A., from the date of filing the
complaint, till realization, besides payment of cost and compliance of other directions, contained in
Clause (i) above.
v.   Any other relief granted, and direction given
by the District Forum, which is contrary to, or in variance with this order,
subject to the modification, aforesaid, shall stand set aside.
25.  
 Certified
copies of this order, be sent to the parties, free of charge.
26.  
 The file be consigned to Record Room,
after completion 

 

Pronounced.
26/11/2013 

 

Sd/-
